headline: Russia hides refinery data, Gulf naphtha skirts Hormuz, Qatar LNG FM to end-Nov
hook: Russia has made refinery, contract and tanker-route data off-limits to public reporting. Qatar's LNG force majeure now runs to end-November, and Reuters reports UAE and Kuwait naphtha is sidestepping Hormuz.
board: Hormuz leads with 7 signals and 7-day pressure of 45 (48 prior). Red Sea & Suez rose to 10 from 6, while Gulf of Aden eased to 2 from 16.
question: Now that Russian refinery and tanker-route data is off-limits, which sources will you use to track Russian product cargoes?

items.headline: Putin decree puts Russian refinery and export data off-limits
items.statLabel: Russian refinery throughput by June, IEA, down 30% y/y
items.what: Reuters reports that a decree Putin signed Monday bars public reporting of refinery production, export contract details, shipping routes and vessel coordinates at export terminals. The only exception is a company disclosing its own figures.
items.why: Buyers and charterers lose public data on Russian product volumes, buyers and routes. Oilprice.com links the decree to sanctions enforcement: the less the West can verify, the harder the price cap is to police.
facts: Customs statistics and planned sales volumes on commodity exchanges fall under the same rule
Ukrainian drones hit a Russian refinery every three days on average in Jan-Aug 2026
Gasoline output is down about 20% and diesel nearly 30%; shortages reported in 92% of regions
items.watch: Whether companies use the self-disclosure exception, and Reuters' reporting that Russian oil supply to India is tightening on reduced exports and strong Chinese demand.

items.headline: UAE and Kuwait lift naphtha exports to Asia, sidestepping Hormuz
items.statLabel: Gulf exporters named: UAE and Kuwait
items.what: MarineLink and Reuters report that the UAE and Kuwait have increased naphtha exports to Asia. Reuters, citing sources, says the flows sidestep the Strait of Hormuz.
items.why: This affects Gulf products going to Asia on the Hormuz lane. The reports give no volumes, routes or costs, so the size of the shift cannot be measured from today's material.
facts: Reuters bases the account on unnamed sources
Oilprice.com says neighbouring Gulf exporters have shipped oil secretly out of Hormuz
Hormuz logged 7 signals on the scan day, the most of any lane
items.watch: Whether follow-up reports put volumes or routes on the UAE and Kuwait naphtha flows. None are given in today's material.

items.headline: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure to end-November
items.statLabel: Qatar LNG cargoes exported, same period a year apart
items.what: Bloomberg sources say QatarEnergy extended force majeure to end-November, from end-October, for buyers in Bangladesh and Pakistan and at least one in India. Edison says it will get no cargoes until early December.
items.why: Qatari LNG shipments to Asia and Europe through Hormuz stay largely blocked. Oilprice.com cites the continuing US-Iran stalemate over the chokepoint.
facts: Qatar has lost $24bn in sales, with exports down as much as 96%, per Reuters calculations
The force majeure was first issued in April after disruption from the US-Iran war
The 18 vs 509 cargo count comes from ICIS data cited by Reuters
items.watch: The end-November expiry for Asian buyers and Edison's early-December date, and whether QatarEnergy extends again as it did last month.
